# **Data Wrangling**
***

Data wrangling includes cleaning data to fix mistakes and reorganizing data to make it easier to use in visualizations and analyses. 
- [ ] Again, use the {{< glossary "README">}} to identify which file contains commands that wrangle the data. 
- [ ] Open this file and run the code. 

<details> <summary> Click here to see the code included in this file. </summary>

::: {.rcode}
```r
library(dplyr) # for data manipulation
library(stringr) # for working with strings

# load data that we saved in data_import
load("processed_data/sample_metadata.rda")

# clean data
clean_metadata <- sample_metadata %>%
  # remove all rows in data that are missing sample ID
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(SampleID)) %>% 
  # clean study name to only include last name of first author
  mutate(Study = 
           # remove _year from study name
           stringr::str_remove(Study, "\\_.*") %>% 
           # remove first name initial from study name
           stringr::str_remove_all("(?<=.)[A-Z]")) %>% 
  # remove spaces from names of variables 
  dplyr::rename(sampling_paper = `Sampling from papers`, 
         sampling_day = `Sampling, day`) %>%
  # recode "NA" as NA and make sampling_day a numeric variable
  mutate(sampling_day = na_if(sampling_day, "NA") %>%
           as.numeric()) 

# in Yassour study, sample IDs are not unique to samples 
# first inspect this to confirm
clean_metadata %>%
  filter(Study == "Yassour") %>%
  dplyr::select(Study, Category, SampleID, sampling_day) %>%
  head()

# create new unique sample IDs for Yassour study
clean_metadata <- clean_metadata %>%
  # check if study is Yassour
  mutate(SampleID = ifelse(Study == "Yassour", 
                           # if so, combine sample ID and sampling day
                           paste0(SampleID, sampling_day),
                           # if not, leave sample ID as is 
                           SampleID)) 

# confirm that we've fixed this problem
clean_metadata %>%
  filter(Study == "Yassour") %>%
  select(Study, Category, SampleID, sampling_day) %>%
  head()

# two studies (Parnanen and Yassour) took samples 
# from mothers during pregnancy
# remove these samples, because they don't fit into
# the time range that we want to consider 
clean_metadata <- clean_metadata %>%
  filter(!(sampling_paper %in% c("32WK", "Gest")))

# save cleaned data
save(clean_metadata, file = "processed_data/clean_sample_metadata.rda")
```
:::

</details>

Question opportunity
::::
::::{.inner_block}
Now that the data have been wrangled, how many observations remain? And why did we remove data?  

<details> <summary> Hint </summary>

Data are wrangled in the file `02_wrangle_data.R`. You can find out how many rows are in a data frame with the function `nrow(name_of_data_frame)`. You can find out how many columns are in a data frame with the function `ncol(name_of_data_frame)`. If you are working in either RStudio or Positron, you can also see the object dimensions in the Environment pane (in RStudio) or the Session pane (in Positron).

</details>
<details><summary>Answer</summary>

```{r, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
load(here::here("data", "wrangled", "clean_sample_metadata.rda"))
library(dplyr)
```

::: {.rcode}
```{r}
nrow(clean_metadata)
```
:::

There are 1,443 observations after data wrangling. We removed observations that had `NA` values for the variable `SampleID` (in line 10) and we removed observations that were taken before birth (in line 51).

</details>
::::
:::

What are the earliest and latest time points that samples were taken, relative to an infant's birth date, in the data set?  

<details> <summary> Hint </summary>

Data are wrangled in the file `02_wrangle_data.R`. You can use the functions `max()` and `min()` to get the maximum and minimum values in a vector. The variable in the cleaned data set that gives the sampling day relative to the infant's birth date is called `sampling_day`. 

</details>
<details><summary>Answer</summary>

```{r, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
load(here::here("data", "wrangled", "clean_sample_metadata.rda"))
library(dplyr)
```

::: {.rcode}
```{r}
min(clean_metadata$sampling_day, na.rm = TRUE)
max(clean_metadata$sampling_day, na.rm = TRUE)
```
:::

The earliest day that a participant was sampled after birth was 0, and the latest day was 480. 

</details>
